Lock step 1 (Parallelism, Probes, and Q2: 'Equality runs share a window under the lock, with at most four Chromium instances'): this cannot run under the lock form the plan names. `flock FILE CMD` from util-linux 2.39.3 takes an exclusive lock by default, and the J0c form wraps every Chromium-launching command that way (`j0c-brief.md:22, 89, 242-248`). Under that form, equality runs serialize one command at a time and never share a window. If lane M instead holds the lock for the window, every lane command written in the J0c form blocks until the window ends. The window ends only when those commands finish, so the window deadlocks. `flock` also has no count, so nothing enforces 'at most four Chromium instances'. Fix: use two modes on `/home/user/.wave/journey.lock`.
- Every equality run and every CPU-bound command takes `flock -s`. That covers build, check, lint, format, the Node suites, `npm ci`, and the mutation script.
- Each price window takes `flock -x` once and holds it across all its runs and output copies, as in `flock -x /home/user/.wave/journey.lock bash WINDOW_SCRIPT`, where `WINDOW_SCRIPT` is the window's command list. That stops another command from slipping in between J-B0's two runs or before the copies.
- A counting semaphore enforces the four-instance cap: four slot files, each taken with `flock -n` in a retry loop, one slot per project a command launches.
- Sessions outside the unit keep the exclusive J0c form, so they wait through both kinds of window. That matches Q2's 'other lanes' Chromium suites wait'.

Lock step 2 (price windows under shared equality traffic): a price window can wait without bound. Linux `flock` grants a new shared lock while an exclusive request is waiting. Equality runs from two or more lanes that overlap can therefore hold the price window off indefinitely. Fix: add a turnstile file. Every command takes `flock -x` on the turnstile, then its mode lock on `journey.lock`, then releases the turnstile. In bash that is `exec 8>TURNSTILE; flock -x 8; exec 9>/home/user/.wave/journey.lock; flock -s 9; flock -u 8; CMD`. A price window keeps the turnstile until it holds `-x`.

Lock step 3 ('Price runs hold the host alone'): the lock binds only processes that take it, and the Orchestrator's own gate script takes none. `gates.sh:10-12` runs `npm run "$gate"` bare, including `test:journey` and four Chromium suites, and it was running unlocked at 04:33 UTC. Run A overlapped the T4 lane's unlocked acceptance checks from 02:39:16 to 02:44:04 UTC (proposal 3, change 2, basis). No instruction file names the lock: a search for `journey.lock` and `flock` returns nothing in scaffold `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `AGENTS.md`, `lanes.md`, or `plan.md`. Fix: wrap the unit's gate runner in the two-mode lock, and add the lock rule to `lanes.md` § Rules before P0 so that every lane brief on this host carries it.

Measurement plan step 2 and Parallelism ('Lanes write code ... while J-B0 runs, because editing takes no host time'): the premise is false on this host. Lanes run as local agent processes; the Codex launcher records a local pid (`/home/user/.wave/codex/j0c4.launch:1`). This session's own Claude Code process used 1,951 s of CPU in 20,623 s, which is 9.5 percent of one core (`ps`, PID 113, 04:28 UTC). Four writing lanes plus the Orchestrator during P0 can take a share of the 4 cores of the same order as the 40.71 s spread between two runs of one tree. That spread is 4.7 percent of 858.59 s. Acceptance (P6) runs with the lanes idle, so the J-B0 comparison is biased toward the plan. Fix: pause every lane's turns during each price window, including P0. Otherwise, record each window's CPU time outside the run's process tree (`/proc/stat` less the run tree's `/proc/PID/stat` times) and refuse any comparison whose windows differ by more than J-B0's two-run spread.

Memory steps (item 12's placement input, P-J, P5, and acceptance step 11 'peak under 14,345,035,776 bytes'): the sampler does not measure the run. `tmp/codex/j0b-measure.ts:7-12` reads `memory.usage_in_bytes` of the Bash cgroup, and that figure includes page cache.
- With no test running (`total_rss` 3,321,856 bytes), the cgroup read 9,233,301,504 bytes, of which `total_cache` was 8,889,008,128 (`memory.stat`).
- `memory.max_usage_in_bytes` already equals the limit, 14,345,031,680, with `memory.failcnt` at 273,797 and `oom_kill` at 0.
- The live limit is 4,096 bytes under the plan's 14,345,035,776, so the acceptance check 'under 14,345,035,776' always passes.
- A peak compared with the live limit can reach it through cache alone.
- J0c's own control run (0.03 s, no test) read 2,725,822,464 bytes (`tmp/codex/j0c-sampler-control-measurement.json`).

The reading therefore cannot feed item 12 or show coinciding renderer peaks in P-J. Fix: the unit's copy of the sampler records `total_rss + total_shmem` from `memory.stat` (neither is reclaimable without swap). It also records the RSS of each renderer, grouped by browser root process; `oom_kill` from `memory.oom_control` before and after the run; and the live `limit`. P-J and acceptance require an unchanged `oom_kill` and an anonymous peak that leaves room for one more renderer at its measured peak.

Equality windows bounded by instance count: four separate scoped invocations do not match a full run's memory. A full run launches four Chromium instances under one Vitest process; four scoped runs launch four. The `test:setup:browser` invocation sampled at 04:32 UTC held 571 MB RSS in its Vitest process, plus about 610 MB in its browser, network, GPU, zygote, and storage processes, beside its renderers (747, 256, and 63 MB; `ps`). Proposal 3 reads the journey renderers at 1,070,052 to 1,775,380 KB each. Every lane's commands share the one 14,345,031,680-byte cgroup. Fix: bound equality concurrency by the anonymous footprint per invocation that the fixed sampler measures in J-B0, not by instance count. Run the heavy light-1280 preservation and partition work one invocation at a time: lane 0's split run and the equality parts of P-B, P-C, P-D, P-H, and P-I.
